question:
For what values of $k$ does the determinant
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}k & 1 & 1\\1 & k & 1\\1 & 1 & k\end{vmatrix}$$
vanish?

(a) Simplify $D$ using suitable determinant operations.

(b) Determine all real values of $k$ for which $D=0$.

(c) State which of the values obtained is a repeated root.
explanation:
(a)
Apply $R_2\to R_2-R_1$ and $R_3\to R_3-R_1$:
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}k & 1 & 1\\1-k & k-1 & 0\\1-k & 0 & k-1\end{vmatrix}$$
Take $(k-1)$ common from both $R_2$ and $R_3$:
$$D=(k-1)^2\begin{vmatrix}k & 1 & 1\\-1 & 1 & 0\\-1 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
Expanding along the first row,
$$D=(k-1)^2\left[k-(-1)+1\right]$$
$$D=(k-1)^2(k+2)$$

(b)
For $D=0$,
$$(k-1)^2(k+2)=0$$
Therefore,
$$k=1\quad\text{or}\quad k=-2$$

(c)
Since the factor $(k-1)$ occurs twice, $k=1$ is a repeated root. The value $k=-2$ is a simple root.

options.D:
(a) $D=(k-1)(k+1)(k+2)$
(b) $k=1,-1,-2$
(c) None of the roots is repeated
